remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements exclusively (never concatenate user input into SQL).
Apply strict input validation and allow-listing on all query parameters.
Enforce least-privilege database accounts for the application (no DDL/GRANT rights).
Escape special characters if dynamic SQL is unavoidable (defense in depth only).
validation: Verify the affected version is running and the query paths are exposed.
Confirm with a non-destructive proof-of-concept in a staging environment.
Check WAF/IDS rules for SQL injection signatures covering this endpoint.

remediation: Encode all dynamic output in the correct output context (HTML, attribute, URL, JS).
Apply a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) and set HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite cookies.
Sanitize and validate user input server-side; prefer allow-lists over deny-lists.
Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and frame-ancestors headers.
validation: Confirm input is reflected and not encoded in the target context.
Validate CSP header and cookie flags on the affected host.
Run an XSS-specific test payload against the endpoint.

remediation: Never pass user input directly to OS commands; use API libraries or subprocess argument lists.
Apply strict input validation and allow-lists for command parameters.
Run the application under a least-privilege OS account with restricted shell access.
Sanitize and reject metacharacters (; | & $ ` > < etc.) when commands are unavoidable.
validation: Verify that input reaches a command execution sink.
Confirm OS account privileges of the service user.
Test with a benign echo payload in staging.

remediation: Avoid deserialization of untrusted data; prefer safe formats (JSON) and validated schemas.
Use a safe deserialization library and enforce type allow-lists.
Authenticate and integrity-protect serialized data with HMAC or signatures.
Apply vendor patch that addresses the vulnerable deserialization path.
validation: Identify all deserialization entry points (cookies, RPC, AMQP payloads).
Confirm the patch/configuration is applied.
Run a safe deserialization PoC in staging.

remediation: Validate and allow-list all URLs, hostnames, and IPs the application may fetch.
Enforce egress filtering and network segmentation to internal resources.
Disable redirects to internal IP ranges and block metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254).
Use a dedicated proxy with egress allow-lists for outbound requests.
validation: Verify which URLs are reachable from the vulnerable component.
Check egress firewall rules and metadata service access.
Confirm the allow-list is enforced at runtime.

remediation: Disable external entity resolution and DTD processing in the XML parser.
Use a secure parser configuration (e.g., defusedxml for Python).
Validate uploaded content type and reject XML from untrusted sources if possible.
validation: Confirm XML parser configuration disables external entities.
Test with a benign XXE payload in staging.
Verify no sensitive files/URLs can be read.

remediation: Normalize and validate all file paths; reject traversal sequences and absolute paths.
Use a safe chroot/base-directory join that prevents escaping the root.
Enforce read permissions and least privilege on the served directory.
Patch the affected application to the latest vendor release.
validation: Confirm traversal payloads are blocked at the application.
Verify filesystem permissions on served directories.
Test encoded traversal variants (%2e%2e/, ..%2f).

remediation: Implement request rate-limiting and connection/concurrency limits at the service and LB.
Apply the vendor patch or upgrade to a fixed version.
Add load shedding, request timeouts, and resource quotas.
Monitor CPU/memory and enable alerting on anomaly thresholds.
validation: Verify rate limits are enforced at the endpoint.
Confirm the service is upgraded to a patched version.
Load-test the endpoint against the CVE scenario.

remediation: Apply the vendor security patch or upgrade to a non-vulnerable version.
Enable compiler/hardening mitigations (ASLR, NX, stack canaries, FORTIFY_SOURCE).
Validate all buffer sizes and bounds in custom code.
Deploy the affected service behind a network ACL to limit exposure.
validation: Confirm patched version is running.
Verify hardening mitigations are enabled on the binary/host.
Restrict access to the vulnerable service via firewall.

remediation: Enforce strong authentication on all exposed interfaces.
Require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for privileged access.
Apply vendor patch that fixes the authentication bypass.
Audit authentication logs for anomalies.
validation: Confirm the patch addresses the bypass path.
Verify MFA is enforced for the affected service.
Review auth logs for unauthorized access attempts.

remediation: Apply the vendor patch to stop unintended information exposure.
Redact sensitive data in responses, logs, and error messages.
Restrict access to sensitive endpoints via ACLs.
Review application configuration for verbose error handling.
validation: Verify sensitive data is no longer exposed.
Review logs and error pages for sensitive content.
Confirm access controls on the affected endpoint.

remediation: Use modern, approved cryptographic algorithms (AES-256, SHA-256+, ECDSA/RSA-2048+).
Replace broken ciphers and protocols (RC4, MD5, SHA-1, TLS < 1.2).
Upgrade the library/service to a version with fixed crypto defaults.
validation: Audit cipher suites and TLS protocol versions offered.
Verify the crypto library version is patched.
Re-test with a crypto-scanner (e.g., TLS scanner).

remediation: Fix certificate validation in the affected client/server (load proper CA bundle).
Upgrade to a version with corrected TLS verification behavior.
Configure strict TLS 1.2+ with validated certificate chains.
Remove test/self-signed certificates from production.
validation: Verify certificates are valid and trusted.
Confirm TLS version and cipher configuration.
Test connection with an expired/untrusted cert to confirm rejection.

remediation: Validate file type, extension, and content (magic bytes) server-side.
Store uploads outside the web root and serve them via a controlled handler.
Apply the vendor patch or upgrade the affected application.
Scan uploaded files with AV and restrict upload size.
validation: Verify that script execution is disabled in the upload directory.
Confirm file-type validation is enforced.
Attempt uploading a benign test file with a script extension in staging.

remediation: Implement anti-CSRF tokens for all state-changing requests.
Validate Origin/Referer headers on sensitive endpoints.
Set SameSite=Lax/Strict on session cookies.
Require re-authentication for high-impact actions.
validation: Verify CSRF tokens are present and validated.
Confirm SameSite cookie attributes.
Test a cross-origin state-changing request.

remediation: Apply the vendor patch that fixes the privilege escalation.
Run services with least privilege and drop unnecessary capabilities.
Audit permissions on files, services, and sudo entries.
Monitor for unusual privilege elevation events.
validation: Confirm the vulnerable component is patched.
Verify least-privilege configuration.
Check audit logs for privilege escalation attempts.

remediation: Enforce authorization on all server-side endpoints, never rely on client-side checks.
Implement role-based access control (RBAC) and object-level authorization.
Apply the vendor patch or upgrade the application.
Test all access-control paths (direct object reference, missing function-level access).
validation: Confirm authorization checks exist on each endpoint.
Test with an unprivileged account against restricted resources.
Verify RBAC configuration matches the security policy.

remediation: Remove credentials and sensitive data from logs.
Apply the vendor patch that prevents sensitive logging.
Configure log redaction and centralized log retention policies.
Restrict log file permissions to least privilege.
validation: Search logs for credentials/secret patterns.
Verify log file permissions.
Confirm log management is centralized and monitored.

remediation: Apply the vendor security patch or upgrade to a fixed version.
Enable runtime hardening (ASLR, NX, RELRO, stack canaries).
Segment the network to limit access to the vulnerable service.
validation: Confirm patched version is running.
Verify hardening flags and mitigations.
Restrict service exposure via firewall.

remediation: Apply the vendor patch fixing the use-after-free.
Enable hardening mitigations and memory sanitizers in dev.
Restrict network exposure of the affected service.
validation: Confirm patched version is running.
Verify mitigations are enabled.
Test the specific CVE trigger in staging.

remediation: Apply the vendor patch or upgrade to a fixed version.
Validate all index/bounds arithmetic in custom code.
Enable boundary-checking tools during development and CI.
validation: Confirm patched version is running.
Run fuzzing/boundary tests against the component.
Restrict service exposure.

remediation: Sanitize user-controlled data before writing to logs.
Apply the vendor patch if the logging library is affected.
Use structured logging with parameters (not string concatenation).
validation: Verify log injection payloads are neutralized.
Confirm logs do not accept CRLF from user input.

remediation: Use parameterized LDAP queries where supported.
Escape LDAP special characters per RFC 4514/4515.
Validate and allow-list user input against LDAP filters.
validation: Verify LDAP filter injection is blocked.
Confirm escaping is applied to all user-controlled values.

remediation: Apply the vendor patch or upgrade to a fixed version.
Disable user-controlled template evaluation.
Use safe template engines with sandboxing and allow-lists.
validation: Verify template evaluation is disabled for untrusted input.
Confirm the engine is patched.

remediation: Sanitize user input for CR/LF characters before response header use.
Apply the vendor patch or upgrade the web framework.
Use framework-level header-setting APIs only.
validation: Confirm CRLF injection is blocked.
Verify headers are set only through safe APIs.

remediation: Apply the vendor patch that fixes the smuggling weakness.
Normalize request parsing across proxies and backend (HTTP/2 where possible).
Enforce strict Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding handling.
validation: Confirm the proxy and backend use consistent parsing.
Test with smuggling-specific payloads in staging.

remediation: Implement resource limits, quotas, and request size caps.
Add rate limiting at the load balancer and application.
Monitor resource usage and alert on anomalies.
validation: Verify resource limits are enforced.
Load-test the endpoint against exhaustion scenarios.

remediation: Fix resource handle leaks in application code.
Apply the vendor patch if the leak is in a dependency.
Add resource monitoring and graceful degradation.
validation: Confirm no unbounded resource growth under load.
Verify monitoring alerts are configured.

remediation: Use atomic operations and proper locking to eliminate TOCTOU races.
Apply the vendor patch that fixes the race condition.
Use safe temporary-file creation (O_EXCL, unique names).
validation: Confirm atomic operations are used for the affected paths.
Test concurrent access in staging.

remediation: Use atomic filesystem operations (O_NOFOLLOW, O_EXCL, secure temp dirs).
Apply the vendor patch addressing the symlink race.
Restrict write access to the affected directories.
validation: Verify safe symlink handling is enforced.
Confirm directory write permissions are restricted.

remediation: Apply the vendor patch or upgrade the configuration library.
Harden the service configuration to the vendor/CIS recommendations.
Disable unused features, modules, and default accounts.
validation: Verify the patched configuration is active.
Run a configuration benchmark (e.g., CIS scanner).

remediation: Apply the latest vendor security patch or upgrade to a non-vulnerable version.
Restrict network access to the affected service (firewall/ACL least privilege).
Enable runtime hardening and monitoring (IDS/WAF alerts, audit logging).
Review application/OS configuration against the relevant CIS Benchmark.
validation: Confirm the affected version is patched or mitigated.
Verify exposure is reduced (network segmentation, ACLs).
Run a re-scan to confirm the finding is resolved.
